title: Linking Issues, Commits, and PRs
learning_objectives: Use GitHub's closing keywords (Closes, Fixes, Resolves) in PRs to auto-close issues on merge
Use Refs in commit footers to cross-reference without auto-closing
Understand how linking ties together the full workflow: issue → branch → commits → PR → merge
Trace a complete change through GitHub from issue to merged PR
outline: Why linking matters: traceability from business need to code
Closing keywords: Closes #N, Fixes #N, Resolves #N — syntax and behavior
Reference without closing: Refs #N in commit footers
Where to put links: PR description body vs. commit footer
GitHub UI: what happens to an issue when its linked PR merges
Hands-on: Create an issue, make a branch, commit with Refs #N, open PR with Closes #N, merge and verify

helm_context.deliverable: A merged PR that auto-closes a Helm issue via keyword

criteria: Issue created and visible on Helm repo
Branch and commit reference the issue using Refs #N in footer
After merge, the linked issue is automatically closed
Can explain the difference between Closes and Refs

resources.title: Linking a Pull Request to an Issue

professor_constraints: Walk through the full lifecycle in a single hands-on exercise
Show the GitHub UI at each step — issue open, PR linked, issue auto-closed after merge
Use a real (small) Helm improvement as the subject, not a dummy change
